title: Creating & Removing Directories 📁
description: Build and tidy up your filesystem with `mkdir`, `rmdir`, and safe cleanup.

slides.title: Making Directories with mkdir 🏗️
slides.content:
## `mkdir` – Make Directory

Syntax: `mkdir [options] directory_name`

- `mkdir projects` creates a single folder.
- `mkdir -p a/b/c` creates nested directories even if parents don't exist (creates the whole path).
- `mkdir -m 755 dir` sets permissions at creation time.

You can create multiple directories at once: `mkdir docs music pics`.

quizData.question: How do you create a directory named `backup` and a subdirectory `logs` inside it with one command?
quizData.explanation: `-p` creates parent directories as needed. Without it, `mkdir backup/logs` would fail if `backup` doesn't exist.

slides.title: Removing Directories 🗑️
slides.content:
## `rmdir` and `rm -r`

- `rmdir` removes an **empty** directory. Safe but limited.
- `rm -r` removes a directory and everything inside it. **Use with extreme caution!**
- `rm -rf` forces removal without confirmation. `-f` is dangerous; double‑check before using.

Always `ls` the directory first to confirm its contents.

quizData.question: `rmdir` can delete a directory that still contains files.
quizData.explanation: `rmdir` only works on empty directories. For non‑empty ones, use `rm -r`.

slides.title: ⚠️ Danger Zone: rm -rf
slides.content:
## The Nuclear Option

`rm -rf somefolder` irreversibly deletes the folder and all its contents without asking. There is **no trash can**. If you accidentally run `rm -rf /` (as root), you can destroy the whole system.

**Best practice**: Avoid `-f`. Use `rm -ri` to ask for confirmation on each file.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Safer Removal
Use `trash-cli` or `gio trash` to send files to the system trash instead of permanent deletion.
